question.questionText: I finished writing up the report, but ____ hasn’t finished it yet.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
In the sentence 'I finished writing up the report, but ____ hasn’t finished it yet.', the blank needs a subject pronoun because it is the subject of the verb 'hasn't finished'. After 'but', we need a pronoun that can act as the subject of the clause.
  • him (object pronoun): 'Him' is an object pronoun, used as the object of a verb or preposition, not as a subject.
  • he (subject pronoun): 'He' is a subject pronoun, used as the subject of a verb. It is the correct choice here.
  • they (subject pronoun): 'They' is a subject pronoun for plural or singular non-binary, but the sentence context suggests a singular male.
  • her (object pronoun / possessive adjective): 'Her' is an object pronoun or possessive adjective, not used as a subject pronoun.
Related structure or vocabulary: Subject pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they) are used as the subject of a verb. Object pronouns (me, you, him, her, it, us, them) are used as the object of a verb or preposition.
